verdicts.strongest_argument: Both components of the claim are published in the admissible corpus, and the second one is published twice by different people. The Dollar General read-through is docs/2382fb2f...txt line 14, dated 2026-08-27T12:37:04Z: '$OLLI Dollar General earnings beat could mean good news for OLLI' - the exact inference, in the captured feed, six days before the print, on top of a DG print that is among the most widely syndicated retail results of any week. More damaging, the finding's real engine is the asymmetry argument - the pre-print markdown historically not being validated by the print - and that is stated outright by two separate posters in the same admissible document: line 13 (2026-08-27) 'gotta drive it down before earnings so when earnings are good it'll just go back to where it was.. over and over the game goes', and line 15 (2026-08-26) 'typical game in market now.. bring price down before earnings and then good earnings brings it back'. The consensus anchor is also published: line 23, 2026-08-06, 'Wall St is expecting 1.14 EPS for $OLLI Q2'. Separately, the statistical claim (downside never worse than -3.98%, upside twice above 8%) is not a corpus discovery at all - it is the sealed baseline's own history.moves array, computed from EDGAR acceptance times, visible to every reader of this run and to anyone with a chart. And the size check bounds the whole thing: this name's median reaction across seven prints is 1.80% with a 1.50% deadband, so even a fully correct asymmetry read is worth roughly a percentage point on a $4.3bn stock. The 13G/A filings are passive institutional forms on EDGAR, and passive 13G amendments are as often mechanical rebalancing as conviction adds. I withhold 25 points honestly: the capture has no sell-side preview, no news document and no company disclosure in August, so I cannot check whether the drawdown reflected a downward estimate revision the print would then meet - and the corpus's silence on that is a capture artefact, not a concession. The hunter is also candid that this is weak, which I credit.

prior_publication.what_it_says: 'Dollar General earnings beat could mean good news for OLLI' - the peer read-through, published six days pre-print in the captured feed.
Two separate posters articulate the pre-print-markdown-then-recovery asymmetry that is the finding's stated reason for signing positive.
Relays a $1.14 Q2 EPS consensus, so a consensus figure was in circulation in the capture (with, as the hunter notes, a wrong 08/27 report date).
The two SCHEDULE 13G/A filings are public EDGAR forms with timestamped acceptances.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Admissible bars only (clean-view excludes the 2026-09-02 bar and snapshot 20260902T150727Z; the baseline correctly stops at the 2026-09-01 close of 72.34, so it is not reading the reaction). Run-up is -3.04% over five sessions and -6.17% over twenty on a 1.42m-share average - a slow drift, not a capitulation. The decisive number is the reaction distribution itself: seven prints with a 1.80% median absolute move, five up, worst outcome -3.98%. Whatever this claim is worth, it is worth about one percent, because that is the entire size of this name's earnings reaction. Baseline quality is sound (fits_cadence), so no defective anchor is inflating the size.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated pre-print source showing sell-side Q2 estimates had been cut into the drawdown while the DG datapoint implied they were too low, giving the asymmetry a quantified gap rather than a chart pattern; or a reaction history where the median move was large enough for a one-percent asymmetry edge to matter.

interactions: The main claim and its 'independence' corroboration are drawn from the same admissible StockTwits document plus the same filings.json index, so they are one source cluster; the Fidelity +29% detail is a retail relay with no filing body behind it in the capture.
corpus_limits: Per clean-view/OLLI.json I excluded snapshot 20260902T150727Z and the 2026-09-02 bar - for a bmo print the event-day close is the reaction, so nothing from 09-02 entered my reasoning. OLLI's capture holds no news items and no analyst previews, so I could not verify DG's actual results, estimate revisions into the print, or whether any broker published an OLLI preview; I have marked that as a capture artefact rather than scoring it. No options chain, so no implied move.
